docs.title: GLORA: Global Events Analysis with LangChain
docs.text:
Conversational Intelligence for Global Events Data

View on GitHub

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
GLORA (Global ??? Analysis) is a powerful tool for analyzing and querying global events using natural language. It combines LangChain's conversational AI capabilities with vector embeddings to provide semantic search and conversational analysis of event datasets.

Designed for researchers, analysts, and developers who need to extract insights from massive global event datasets without writing complex SQL queries or manual data analysis.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Global event databases contain millions of records with complex relationships. Traditional analysis requires:

  • Deep knowledge of database schemas
  • Complex SQL queries for pattern matching
  • Manual correlation of related events
  • Time-consuming exploratory data analysis

docs.title: The Solution
docs.text:
A natural language interface powered by LangChain and vector embeddings that allows users to:

  • Ask questions in plain English: "What events in Africa involved cybersecurity in 2023?"
  • Get semantic matches: Understands synonyms and related concepts
  • Conversational follow-ups: Build on previous queries with context
  • Fast vector search: Millions of records in milliseconds

docs.title: LangChain Ollama Conversational Agent
docs.text:
Privacy-First AI Assistant with Tool-Augmented Reasoning

View on GitHub 1 Star

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A production-grade conversational agent that runs entirely on your local machine. Built with LangChain and Ollama, it combines the power of large language models with practical tools like web search, weather, and date retrieval - all without sending your data to the cloud.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Cloud-based AI services have limitations:

  • 💰 Expensive: API costs add up quickly with usage
  • 🔒 Privacy risks: Your conversations and data leave your machine
  • 🌐 Internet dependency: Requires constant connectivity
  • 📊 Data concerns: Your prompts may be used for training

docs.title: The Solution
docs.text:
Run powerful LLMs locally with tool integration:

  • ✅ Zero API costs after initial setup
  • ✅ Complete data privacy - everything stays on your machine
  • ✅ Works offline (except for tools requiring internet)
  • ✅ Full control over model selection and parameters

docs.title: Tool-Augmented Reasoning
docs.text:
The agent can invoke external tools when needed:

Tool Purpose Example Query DuckDuckGo Search Web search for current information "What's the latest news about AI?" Weather Real-time weather data "What's the weather in San Diego?" Date/Time Current date and time "What day of the week is it?"

The agent intelligently decides when to use tools vs when to answer from its internal knowledge.

Agent: [Explains Python programming]

docs.text:

docs.title: Agent Design
docs.text:
ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) pattern:

  1. Thought: Agent reasons about what to do
  2. Action: Decides to use a tool or answer directly
  3. Observation: Processes tool output
  4. Final Answer: Generates response
# Example agent reasoning
Thought: User wants weather info, I need to use the weather tool
Action: weather("San Diego")
Observation: Temperature: 72°F, Conditions: Sunny
Final Answer: It's currently 72°F and sunny in San Diego!

docs.text:

Run the agent:

streamlit run app.py

The UI will open in your browser, and all inference happens locally!

docs.title: Neural Network from Scratch
docs.text:
Educational Deep Dive into Neural Network Fundamentals

View on GitHub

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A comprehensive educational implementation of neural networks using only Python and NumPy - no deep learning frameworks. This project progressively builds from a single neuron to multi-layer networks with various optimization algorithms, providing deep insights into how neural networks actually work under the hood.

docs.title: The Learning Journey
docs.text:
Understanding neural networks at a fundamental level requires going beyond high-level APIs. This project deliberately avoids TensorFlow and PyTorch to expose the mathematical foundations:

  • Forward propagation: How inputs transform into predictions
  • Backpropagation: The calculus behind learning
  • Optimization: Different strategies for updating weights
  • Regularization: Preventing overfitting

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text: The implementation follows a progressive complexity approach, with each module building on the previous:

docs.title: Level 1: Single Neuron
docs.text: File Concept Key Learning neuron.py Basic neuron Forward pass, weight initialization backprop_single_neuron.py Training single neuron Gradient descent, backpropagation basics

docs.title: Level 2: Single Layer
docs.text: File Concept Key Learning dense_layer.py Dense layer implementation Matrix multiplication, vectorization backprop_layer.py Layer backpropagation Chain rule, gradient computation

docs.title: Level 3: Multi-Layer Networks
docs.text: File Concept Key Learning backprop_multiple_layer.py Deep networks Gradient flow through layers dense_layer_with_optimiser.py Basic optimizer Momentum, learning rate

docs.title: Level 4: Advanced Optimizers
docs.text: File Optimizer Key Feature dense_layer_with_Adagrad.py AdaGrad Adaptive learning rates dense_layer_with_RMSprop.py RMSprop Moving average of gradients dense_layer_with_ADAM.py Adam Combines momentum + RMSprop

docs.title: Level 5: Regularization
docs.text: File Technique Prevents dense_layer_with_ADAM_Regularizer.py L1/L2 regularization Weight explosion dense_layer_with_ADAM_Regularizer_dropout.py Dropout Co-adaptation

docs.title: Forward Propagation
docs.text:
# Simple forward pass (conceptual)
def forward(X, weights, bias):
    # Linear transformation
    z = np.dot(X, weights) + bias
    # Activation (ReLU)
    a = np.maximum(0, z)
    return a

docs.title: Backpropagation
docs.text:
The chain rule in action:

∂Loss/∂weight = ∂Loss/∂output × ∂output/∂z × ∂z/∂weight

Each module implements this manually to reveal the mathematics.

docs.title: Optimizer Comparison
docs.text: Optimizer Learning Rate Momentum Adaptive Best For SGD Fixed ❌ ❌ Simple problems Momentum Fixed ✅ ❌ Smooth convergence AdaGrad Adaptive ❌ ✅ Sparse gradients RMSprop Adaptive ❌ ✅ Non-stationary Adam Adaptive ✅ ✅ General purpose

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text:
• NumPy: All matrix operations and mathematics
  • Python: Core implementation language
  • Matplotlib: Loss curve visualization (optional)

docs.title: Mathematical Foundations
docs.text:
Activation Functions:

  • ReLU: f(x) = max(0, x)
  • Sigmoid: f(x) = 1 / (1 + e^(-x))
  • Tanh: f(x) = (e^x - e^(-x)) / (e^x + e^(-x))

Loss Functions:

  • MSE: L = (1/n) Σ(y - ŷ)²
  • Cross-Entropy: L = -Σ y·log(ŷ)

Regularization:

  • L1: R = λΣ|w| (encourages sparsity)
  • L2: R = λΣw² (prevents large weights)

docs.title: Conceptual Understanding
docs.text:
1. Why backpropagation works: Not just what, but why
  2. Gradient flow: How gradients propagate through layers
  3. Vanishing gradients: Why deep networks are challenging
  4. Optimization landscape: Local minima, saddle points

docs.title: Practical Skills
docs.text:
1. NumPy proficiency: Efficient matrix operations
  2. Debugging ML: Understanding what goes wrong
  3. Algorithm implementation: Translating math to code
  4. Performance optimization: Vectorization techniques

docs.text:
# Initialize a dense layer

# Forward pass

# Backward pass

# Update weights with Adam
optimizer = AdamOptimizer(learning_rate=0.001)
optimizer.update(layer.weights, gradients)

docs.text:

Optimizer Convergence Speed Final Accuracy Stability SGD Slow 92% Variable Momentum Medium 94% Good Adam Fast 96% Excellent Adam + L2 + Dropout Fast 97% Excellent

docs.text:

  2. Regularization helps: L2 + dropout prevents overfitting
  3. Learning rate critical: Too high causes divergence, too low is slow
  4. Initialization impacts: Good initialization speeds up training

docs.title: Part-of-Speech Tagging
docs.text:
NLP Project for Linguistic Analysis

View on GitHub 1 Star

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
An implementation of Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging for natural language processing. This project demonstrates core NLP techniques for analyzing text structure and extracting linguistic patterns.

POS tagging is a fundamental NLP task that assigns grammatical categories (noun, verb, adjective, etc.) to each word in a sentence, enabling downstream applications like named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and machine translation.

docs.title: What is POS Tagging?
docs.text:
Part-of-Speech tagging labels each word with its grammatical role:

Example:

Input:  "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
Output: DET ADJ  ADJ   NOUN VERB PREP DET ADJ  NOUN
        The quick brown fox  jumps over the  lazy dog

docs.title: Common POS Tags

docs.title: YouTube Shorts AI Agent
docs.text:
Autonomous Content Generation with Multi-Agent Architecture

View on GitHub

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: An intelligent multi-agent system that transforms a simple topic request into a production-ready YouTube Shorts concept. Built with Google's Agent Developer Kit (ADK) and Gemini 2.0, it autonomously researches trends, writes scripts, validates viral potential, and generates detailed visual directions.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text: Content creation is time-consuming and requires constant trend awareness. Creators spend hours researching what's trending, brainstorming ideas, writing scripts, and planning visuals. This agent automates the entire ideation process while ensuring the content has viral potential.

docs.title: The Solution
docs.text:
A sequential chain of specialized AI agents that collaborate to produce high-quality video concepts:

  1. Research trending topics using real-time Google Trends data
  2. Write initial script based on trending insights
  3. Validate viral potential through a quality scoring loop
  4. Refine script iteratively until it meets quality thresholds
  5. Visualize detailed shot-by-shot visual directions
  6. Format final output as production-ready markdown

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[User Input: Topic] --> B[MemoryCoordinator]
    B --> C[Researcher Agent]
    C --> |Google Trends MCP| D[Get Trending Data]
    D --> E[ScriptWriter Agent]
    E --> F[Quality Loop]
    F --> G[StateInitializer]
    G --> H[ViralityJudge]
    H --> |Score < 8| I[ScriptRefiner]
    I --> |Iteration < 3| H
    H --> |Score ≥ 8| J[Exit Loop]
    J --> K[Visualizer Agent]
    K --> L[Formatter Agent]
    L --> M[Final Output: Production Plan]

    style F fill:#667eea,stroke:#764ba2,stroke-width:3px,color:#fff
    style D fill:#f093fb,stroke:#764ba2,stroke-width:2px
    style M fill:#2dd4bf,stroke:#14b8a6,stroke-width:2px

docs.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
docs.text:
8 specialized agents working in sequence, each with a focused responsibility:

Agent Purpose Model MemoryCoordinator Future-ready context management gemini-2.0-flash Researcher Fetches trending topics via Google Trends MCP gemini-2.0-flash ScriptWriter Drafts initial script from trending insights gemini-2.0-flash StateInitializer Prevents context errors in quality loop gemini-2.0-flash ViralityJudge Scores content engagement (0-10 scale) gemini-2.0-flash ScriptRefiner Iterates based on feedback gemini-2.0-flash Visualizer Creates shot-by-shot visual direction gemini-2.0-flash-lite Formatter Produces markdown table output gemini-2.0-flash-lite

docs.title: Google Trends Integration via MCP
docs.text:
What is MCP?

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard for connecting AI models to external data sources. It allows agents to call custom tools and APIs in a standardized way.

This project implements a custom MCP server (mcp_server.py) that exposes Google Trends data:

  • Real-time trending searches from Google Trends RSS feed
  • Interest over time analysis
  • Related queries discovery
  • Async tool implementation for seamless ADK integration

The mcp_client_tool.py wraps the MCP server as an ADK FunctionTool, enabling the Researcher agent to access live trend data.

docs.title: Smart Quality Loop
docs.text:
A self-correcting mechanism ensures viral potential:

# Quality Loop Flow
while iterations < 3:
    score = ViralityJudge.evaluate(script)
    if score >= 8:
        exit_loop()  # Quality threshold met
    else:
        script = ScriptRefiner.improve(script, feedback)
  • Maximum 3 iterations to prevent infinite loops
  • Score threshold of 8/10 for viral potential
  • Automatic refinement based on structured feedback
  • Tool-based exit using exit_loop() function

docs.text:

  • gemini-2.0-flash-lite: Text-only agents (Visualizer, Formatter)
